title: Epidemiology of Human Metapneumovirus Infection-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a globally circulating respiratory pathogen. The objective of this systematic review is to evaluate the prevalence, case fatality rate, age-related severity, and seasonality of hMPV in the group of Acute Respiratory Infections (ARIs) and Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP). METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of articles on hMPV published from January 2001 to June 2025. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we systematically searched PubMed and ScienceDirect for eligible articles using strict inclusion and exclusion criteria. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed to estimate pooled prevalence, and subgroup analyses were conducted by study group, geographic region, COVID-19 period, and age group. RESULTS: One hundred one studies met the inclusion criteria, of which 96 contributed to the meta-analysis. The pooled global prevalence of hMPV was 6% (95% CI: 5%-7%). Prevalence estimates were highest in patients with respiratory tract infections (RTIs) patients (6%) and in South America (10%). Age-stratified analysis showed a high prevalence in children under 5 years (7%). Seroprevalence studies demonstrated low hMPV antibody prevalence in young children less than 1 year. The case fatality rate ranged from 2.5% in elderly populations to 4.4% in severe pediatric cases. hMPV mainly affects children under 2 years, with a smaller burden in older adults. Seasonal peaks were typically observed in late winter to early spring. CONCLUSION: hMPV remains an important cause of respiratory disease worldwide, with a disproportionate burden on children. The significant heterogeneity across studies and evidence of publication bias highlight the need for standardized surveillance.

title: Computational prediction of a multi-epitope Human Metapneumovirus vaccine candidate through integrated reverse vaccinology and pan-genomic approaches
abstract: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a primary cause of global respiratory infections yet no approved vaccine currently exists. This study computationally predicts a multi-epitope vaccine candidate using a diverse dataset of 65 HMPV sequences spanning five continents. Following the screening of lead proteins for antigenicity and virulence, fifteen highly conserved MHC-I, MHC-II and B-cell epitopes were prioritized. These were integrated with a putative L7/L12 adjuvant using optimized AAY, GPGPG, and KK linkers to design three constructs (HMPV_V1–V3). Structural validation identified HMPV-V2 as the lead candidate that exhibits a Z-score of-5.24 and 87.7% of residues in favored Ramachandran regions indicating excellent stereochemical quality and structural stability. In silico docking indicated a strong predicted binding affinity between HMPV-V2 and the TLR4 receptor (energy: −969.2). Immune simulations predicted a robust adaptive response characterized by high IgG1 titers, memory B-cell maturation, and a Th1-dominant cytokine profile. Furthermore, molecular dynamics simulations suggested exceptional structural integrity for HMPV-V2, maintaining a low RMSD of 8.213 and RMSF of 0.737 throughout the simulation. Optimized in silico cloning into the pET28a (+) vector indicated a high potential for protein expression in E. While these findings provide a theoretically grounded blueprint for vaccine development, this study is entirely computational and lacks experimental validation. Further in vitro and in vivo testing is required to confirm the actual safety and immunogenicity of the proposed candidate.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to computationally predict a multi-epitope vaccine candidate for human metapneumovirus (HMPV) due to the lack of an approved vaccine for this primary cause of global respiratory infections.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a diverse dataset of 65 HMPV sequences spanning five continents to computationally predict a multi-epitope vaccine candidate.
analysis.methods: Following the screening of lead proteins for antigenicity and virulence, fifteen highly conserved MHC-I, MHC-II, and B-cell epitopes were prioritized and integrated with a putative L7/L12 adjuvant using optimized linkers to design three constructs (HMPV_V1–V3).
analysis.main_results: Three vaccine constructs (HMPV_V1–V3) were designed, and HMPV-V2 was identified as the lead candidate with excellent structural quality and stability, strong predicted binding affinity to the TLR4 receptor, and robust immune simulation results.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest a potential vaccine candidate for HMPV, which could inform future surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is entirely computational and lacks experimental validation, limiting confidence in the actual safety and immunogenicity of the proposed candidate.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to computationally predict a multi-epitope vaccine candidate for human metapneumovirus (HMPV) due to the lack of an approved vaccine for this primary cause of global respiratory infections.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study used a diverse dataset of 65 HMPV sequences spanning five continents to computationally predict a multi-epitope vaccine candidate.
analysis_en.methods: Following the screening of lead proteins for antigenicity and virulence, fifteen highly conserved MHC-I, MHC-II, and B-cell epitopes were prioritized and integrated with a putative L7/L12 adjuvant using optimized linkers to design three constructs (HMPV_V1–V3).
analysis_en.main_results: Three vaccine constructs (HMPV_V1–V3) were designed, and HMPV-V2 was identified as the lead candidate with excellent structural quality and stability, strong predicted binding affinity to the TLR4 receptor, and robust immune simulation results.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted HMPV-V2 as the lead candidate due to its structural and immunological properties, providing a theoretically grounded blueprint for vaccine development.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest a potential vaccine candidate for HMPV, which could inform future surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is entirely computational and lacks experimental validation, limiting confidence in the actual safety and immunogenicity of the proposed candidate.

title_zh: 通过集成反向疫苗学和泛基因组方法计算预测多表位 人偏肺病毒 疫苗 候选者
source_body_en: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a primary cause of global respiratory infections yet no approved vaccine currently exists. This study computationally predicts a multi-epitope vaccine candidate using a diverse dataset of 65 HMPV sequences spanning five continents. Following the screening of lead proteins for antigenicity and virulence, fifteen highly conserved MHC-I, MHC-II and B-cell epitopes were prioritized. These were integrated with a putative L7/L12 adjuvant using optimized AAY, GPGPG, and KK linkers to design three constructs (HMPV_V1–V3). Structural validation identified HMPV-V2 as the lead candidate that exhibits a Z-score of-5.24 and 87.7% of residues in favored Ramachandran regions indicating excellent stereochemical quality and structural stability. In silico docking indicated a strong predicted binding affinity between HMPV-V2 and the TLR4 receptor (energy: −969.2). Immune simulations predicted a robust adaptive response characterized by high IgG1 titers, memory B-cell maturation, and a Th1-dominant cytokine profile. Furthermore, molecular dynamics simulations suggested exceptional structural integrity for HMPV-V2, maintaining a low RMSD of 8.213 and RMSF of 0.737 throughout the simulation. Optimized in silico cloning into the pET28a (+) vector indicated a high potential for protein expression in E. While these findings provide a theoretically grounded blueprint for vaccine development, this study is entirely computational and lacks experimental validation. Further in vitro and in vivo testing is required to confirm the actual safety and immunogenicity of the proposed candidate.
abstract_zh: 人偏肺病毒 (HMPV) 是全球呼吸道感染的主要原因,但目前尚无批准的 疫苗。这项研究使用跨越五大洲的 65 个 HMPV 序列的多样化数据集,通过计算预测了多表位 疫苗 候选者。在筛选先导蛋白的抗原性和毒力后,优先考虑了 15 个高度保守的 MHC-I、MHC-II 和 B 细胞表位。使用优化的 AAY、GPPGG 和 KK 连接子将它们与假定的 L7/L12 佐剂整合,设计出三种构建体 (HMPV_V1–V3)。结构验证将 HMPV-V2 确定为主要候选者,其 Z 得分为 5.24,并且 87.7% 的残基位于有利的 Ramachandran 区域,表明具有出色的立体化学质量和结构稳定性。计算机对接表明 HMPV-V2 和 TLR4 受体之间有很强的预测结合亲和力(能量:-969.2)。免疫模拟预测了强烈的适应性反应,其特征是高 IgG1 滴度、记忆 B 细胞成熟和 Th1 主导的细胞因子谱。此外,分子动力学模拟表明 HMPV-V2 具有出色的结构完整性,在整个模拟过程中保持了 8.213 的低 RMSD 和 0.737 的 RMSF。经过计算机优化克隆到 pET28a (+) 媒介 中,表明大肠杆菌中蛋白质表达具有很高的潜力。虽然这些发现为 疫苗 的开发提供了理论上的蓝图,但这项研究完全是计算性的,缺乏实验验证。需要进一步的体外和体内测试来确认拟议候选药物的实际安全性和免疫原性。

title: HUMAN METAPNEUMOVIRUS: AN EMERGING THREAT WITH PANDEMIC POTENTIAL
abstract: H uman metapneumovirus has gained global attention due to recent upsurge in cases reported in China.International travel and trade raise concerns about the potential spread of the 1 virus to the rest of the world.Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) was first identified in 2001 and has been a common cause of acute respiratory infections.It can cause both upper and lower respiratory tract infections and affects all age groups.Infants, children, older adults and people with low immunity are at high risk and can develop complications.Morbidity and mortality remain high in high-risk groups and hospitalized 2 patients.HMPV is an RNA virus of paramyxovirus family with two main subtypes, A and B. The virus lacks a hemagglutinin-neuraminidase protein, making it unique.
journal: JAIMC Journal of Allama Iqbal Medical College

title: Estimating cumulative incidence from partially missing time series of respiratory viral infections
abstract: BACKGROUND: Seasonal respiratory viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV), are major contributors to global respiratory infection burden. Estimating viral incidence using real-world data (RWD) is challenging as misalignment of data collection with seasonal circulation can lead to underestimated incidence and hinder inter-study comparisons. METHODS: We developed a regression-based approach to retrospectively correct partial-season time series with contiguous missing weeks at the start or end of a season. Weekly RSV clinical incidence (per 100,000) was extracted from U.S. RWD sources (Optum® CDM and PharMetrics Plus, adults ≥65 years; Kaiser Permanente Northwest [KPNW], all ages) for seasons 2018-19 to 2023-24 and aligned to RSV‐Net hospitalization surveillance. Weekly early- and late-season missingness scenarios were created (approximately 10%, 15%, 20%, and 25% of weeks removed). Models were fit within each season using harmonic terms and the surveillance-aligned covariate. Uncertainty was quantified using moving block bootstrap 95% prediction intervals. Weekly accuracy was evaluated using RMSE and normalized RMSE, and seasonal burden reconstruction accuracy using cumulative percent error and signed difference. abstract_zh: 背景:季节性呼吸道病毒,包括呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)和人偏肺病毒(hMPV),是全球呼吸道感染负担的主要贡献者。使用真实世界数据 (RWD) 估计病毒 发病率 具有挑战性,因为数据收集与季节性循环的不一致可能导致 发病率 被低估并阻碍研究间比较。方法:我们开发了一种基于回归的方法来回顾性地纠正在赛季开始或结束时连续缺失几周的部分赛季时间序列。每周 RSV 临床 发病率(每 100,000 人)从美国 RWD 来源(Optum® CDM 和 PharMetrics Plus,成人≥65 岁;Kaiser Permanente Northwest [KPNW],所有年龄)中提取 2018-19 至 2023-24 季节,并与 RSV-Net 住院情况 监测 保持一致。创建了每周早季和晚季缺失情景(大约删除了 10%、15%、20% 和 25% 的周)。使用调和项和 监测 对齐协变量在每个季节内拟合模型。使用移动块引导 95% 预测区间来量化不确定性。使用 RMSE 和归一化 RMSE 评估每周准确性,并使用累积百分比误差和符号差评估季节性负担重建准确性。对于 hMPV,我们使用 Optum® CDM(≥65 岁的成人;2022-23 和 2023-24)和 NREVSS 测试阳性评估了说明性扩展;因为积极性是有限的并且取决于测试量,所以我们使用了分母感知的二项式/logit 模型(测试中的积极性)。结果:对于 RSV,每周预测误差随着缺失水平的增加而增加,而重建的季节性负担通常仍接近适用场景中观察到的总数。在 Optum® CDM 和 PharMetrics Plus 中,与季末差距相比,季初差距与更大的累积误差相关,而季末中位误差百分比在缺失水平上接近于零。适用性降低主要是因为 KPNW 由于峰值重叠而造成早季缺失率较高(例如,早期 25% 的情景不适用)。对于 hMPV 测试阳性(说明性;两个季节),每周预测 RMSE 在缺失情况下约为 1-2 个百分点。结论:在多个 RSV 季节和数据源中,当缺失仅限于连续的早季或晚季周且不与高峰活动重叠时,重建的季节性负担通常与观察到的总数一致。这种方法提供了一种透明的方法来提高部分季节呼吸道病毒时间序列的实用性和可比性。然而,当高峰周缺失时,适用性就会降低,并且考虑到有限的季节和测试阳性的使用,hMPV 的结果具有说明性。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决由于数据收集与季节性循环不一致而导致呼吸道病毒 发病率 被低估的挑战,重点关注呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和 人偏肺病毒 (hMPV)。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用基于回归的方法来校正来自美国 RWD 来源(Optum® CDM 和 PharMetrics Plus,成人≥65 岁;Kaiser Permanente Northwest [KPNW],所有年龄)的 2018-19 至 2023-24 季节的部分季节时间序列数据,与 RSV-Net 住院情况 监测 保持一致。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员开发了一种方法来纠正部分季节时间序列数据,方法是创建早季和晚季缺失场景(删除 10%、15%、20% 和 25% 的周)并使用调和项和 监测 对齐协变量拟合模型。使用移动块引导 95% 预测区间量化不确定性,并使用 RMSE 和归一化 RMSE 进行每周预测以及累积百分比误差和季节性负荷重建的符号差来评估准确性。
analysis_zh.main_results: 对于 RSV,每周预测误差随着缺失水平的增加而增加,但重建的季节性负担通常仍接近适用场景中观察到的总数。对于 hMPV,每周预测 RMSE 在缺失情况下约为 1-2 个百分点。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究提供了一种透明的方法来提高部分季节呼吸道病毒时间序列的实用性和可比性,其适用性降低主要是因为 KPNW 由于峰值重叠而导致早期季节缺失较高。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该方法可以增强部分季节呼吸道病毒时间序列的实用性和可比性,有助于呼吸道感染的 监测、诊断 和 治疗。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括在高峰周缺失时适用性降低,以及由于季节有限和使用测试阳性而导致 hMPV 结果的说明性。

title: Emerging Trends in the Pathogenesis, Diagnosis, and Management of Human Metapneumovirus-Associated Respiratory Infections
abstract: Introduction: Human Metapneumovirus is a significant respiratory pathogen causing infections across all age groups, particularly in young children, immunocompromised individuals, and the elderly. Despite its clinical relevance, there are currently no approved vaccines or specific antiviral treatments for Human Metapneumovirus, necessitating further research into therapeutic and preventive strategies. Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed journals, clinical trials, and recent studies focusing on Human Metapneumovirus infection. Data were extracted and analyzed to evaluate the effectiveness of antiviral therapies, monoclonal antibodies, immunomodulators, and vaccine candidates. Results: Studies indicate that Human Metapneumovirus primarily targets the respiratory epithelium, triggering immune responses that contribute to both viral clearance and disease pathogenesis. Investigational therapies, including fusion inhibitors and protease inhibitors, show promise but require further validation. Immunomodulatory agents and herbal remedies may offer supportive benefits, but their efficacy against Human Metapneumovirus remains unproven. Advances in vaccine development are ongoing, with several candidates in preclinical and early clinical stages. Discussion: HMPV continues to pose a substantial public health burden due to its seasonal outbreaks, clinical similarity to other respiratory viruses, and absence of specific therapies. The virus evades immune responses via multiple mechanisms, contributing to disease severity, particularly in vulnerable populations. Although supportive care is currently the mainstay, emerging antivirals and vaccines may offer future solutions. Improved diagnostic access, public awareness, and targeted research are essential for controlling HMPV infections. Conclusion: Human Metapneumovirus continues to pose a public health challenge due to the lack of targeted treatments and vaccines. Ongoing research into antiviral agents, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines is critical for effective disease management. Further clinical trials are needed to establish safe and effective therapeutic options.

title_zh: 发病机制、诊断 和 人偏肺病毒 相关呼吸道感染管理的新趋势
source_body_en: Introduction: Human Metapneumovirus is a significant respiratory pathogen causing infections across all age groups, particularly in young children, immunocompromised individuals, and the elderly. Despite its clinical relevance, there are currently no approved vaccines or specific antiviral treatments for Human Metapneumovirus, necessitating further research into therapeutic and preventive strategies. Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed journals, clinical trials, and recent studies focusing on Human Metapneumovirus infection. Data were extracted and analyzed to evaluate the effectiveness of antiviral therapies, monoclonal antibodies, immunomodulators, and vaccine candidates. Results: Studies indicate that Human Metapneumovirus primarily targets the respiratory epithelium, triggering immune responses that contribute to both viral clearance and disease pathogenesis. Investigational therapies, including fusion inhibitors and protease inhibitors, show promise but require further validation. Immunomodulatory agents and herbal remedies may offer supportive benefits, but their efficacy against Human Metapneumovirus remains unproven. Advances in vaccine development are ongoing, with several candidates in preclinical and early clinical stages. Discussion: HMPV continues to pose a substantial public health burden due to its seasonal outbreaks, clinical similarity to other respiratory viruses, and absence of specific therapies. The virus evades immune responses via multiple mechanisms, contributing to disease severity, particularly in vulnerable populations. Although supportive care is currently the mainstay, emerging antivirals and vaccines may offer future solutions. Improved diagnostic access, public awareness, and targeted research are essential for controlling HMPV infections. Conclusion: Human Metapneumovirus continues to pose a public health challenge due to the lack of targeted treatments and vaccines. Ongoing research into antiviral agents, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines is critical for effective disease management. Further clinical trials are needed to establish safe and effective therapeutic options.
abstract_zh: 引言:人偏肺病毒(HMPV)是一种重要的呼吸道病原体,可在不同年龄段人群中引发感染,尤其是在幼儿、免疫功能低下者及老年人中。尽管其具有重要的临床意义,但目前尚无获批的抗病毒药物或针对人偏肺病毒的特异性治疗方法,亟需进一步研究治疗和预防策略。方法:通过系统性文献综述,检索同行评议期刊、临床试验及近期研究,重点关注人偏肺病毒感染。提取并分析数据,以评估抗病毒药物、单克隆抗体、免疫调节剂及疫苗候选物的有效性。结果:研究表明,人偏肺病毒主要靶向呼吸道上皮细胞,触发免疫应答,这些免疫应答既有助于病毒清除,也会导致疾病发病机制。正在研发的治疗方法,包括融合抑制剂和蛋白酶抑制剂,显示出潜力,但仍需进一步验证。免疫调节剂和中草药可能提供支持性益处,但其对人偏肺病毒的有效性尚未得到证实。疫苗研发取得进展,多个候选疫苗已进入临床前及早期临床阶段。讨论:由于人偏肺病毒的季节性流行、与其他呼吸道病毒的临床相似性以及缺乏特异性治疗方法,该病毒继续对公共卫生构成重大负担。该病毒通过多种机制逃避免疫应答,导致疾病严重程度增加,尤其是在易感人群中。尽管目前主要采用支持性治疗,但新兴的抗病毒药物和疫苗可能为未来提供解决方案。改善诊断可及性、提高公众意识及开展针对性研究对于控制人偏肺病毒感染至关重要。结论:由于缺乏针对性治疗方法和疫苗,人偏肺病毒继续对公共卫生构成挑战。针对抗病毒药物、单克隆抗体及疫苗的持续研究对于有效疾病管理至关重要。亟需进一步临床试验以确立安全有效的治疗方案。

title: Human Metapneumovirus Infection in an Elderly Patient Receiving Maintenance Hemodialysis with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD): A Case Report
abstract: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is an important cause of acute infections of the respiratory system affecting young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Patients suffering from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and end-stage renal disease (ESRD) receiving maintenance hemodialysis represent a particularly vulnerable population, yet published reports describing hMPV infection in dialysis patients remain limited. A 70-year-old male with a background of COPD, hypertension, and diabetic nephropathy with a maintenance hemodialysis regimen presented with a four-day history of fever, cough with rhinorrhea, myalgias, and dyspnea. He was immunized against influenza, COVID-19, and RSV. Physical examination showed signs of mild hypoxemia with diffuse crackles and expiratory wheezing, without evidence of consolidation. The patient’s chest radiograph showed chronic obstructive changes. Triplex RT-PCR for influenza virus, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 was negative. However, a multiplex RT-PCR respiratory panel identified hMPV. He had a good response to supportive care with oxygen supplementation, bronchodilator therapy, and continuation of his scheduled hemodialysis regimen, with subsequent discharge after five days. The above-mentioned case shows how crucial it is to consider the possible hMPV infection in differentiating the cause of respiratory complaints in dialysis patients. This infection, even being a relatively mild one, can have serious consequences from the point of view of infection control in dialysis units due to close contact between patients and their frequent use of common medical devices. This observation highlights the clinical significance of hMPV infections in hemodialysis patients.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 70-year-old male with COPD and end-stage renal disease undergoing maintenance hemodialysis who presented with respiratory symptoms. The patient was found to be infected with human metapneumovirus (hMPV) through a multiplex RT-PCR respiratory panel, while tests for influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 were negative. title: Molecular surveillance of respiratory viruses among outpatients with acute respiratory infections in Yangon, Myanmar, during the 2024 rainy season
abstract: Acute respiratory infections (ARI) remain a major public health problem in Myanmar, a tropical Southeast Asian country, yet comprehensive molecular surveillance data are limited. We conducted outpatient surveillance during the 2024 rainy season and characterized pathogen distribution, seasonality, and viral genetic diversity. From June–November 2024, ARI outpatients were enrolled at two Yangon hospitals. Nasopharyngeal swabs were screened by rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) for influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2. RDT-positive specimens underwent confirmation by real-time PCR (RT-PCR). RDT-negative specimens were tested using the BioFire ® FilmArray ® Respiratory 2.1 Panel (BioFire RP). Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B/Victoria viruses with cycle threshold (Ct) < 32 underwent next-generation sequencing for hemagglutinin (HA) phylogenetics. Human metapneumovirus (hMPV)-positive specimens were sequenced targeting the partial F-gene for genotyping. Among 646 ARI outpatients (median age 3.7 years), at least one pathogen was detected in 548 (84.8%). Of the 331 RDT-positive specimens, influenza A(H3N2) (40.5%), RSV-A (21.5%), and influenza B/Victoria (20.2%) were most frequently detected, alongside a single A(H1N1)pdm09 case (0.3%). Of the 315 RDT-negative specimens analyzed via BioFire RP, rhinovirus/enterovirus (42.5%) and hMPV (15.2%) were the most prevalent. Co-infections were identified in 35 (15.3%) of the 229 BioFire RP-positive specimens. Influenza activity peaked in July–August, while RSV peaked in September. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that influenza A(H3N2) sequences clustered within clades J.2/J.2.1/J.2.2, B/Victoria sequences within V1A.3a.2 (primarily C.5.7), and the single A(H1N1)pdm09 sequence within C.1.9. Notably, partial F-gene sequencing of hMPV revealed a genotype shift from mixed A2/B1 in 2023 to predominantly B2 in 2024. Various respiratory viruses co-circulated during the 2024 rainy season in this setting, displaying distinct seasonal peaks for influenza and RSV. Ongoing viral genetic evolution underscores the need for sustained molecular surveillance.

Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B/Victoria viruses with cycle threshold (Ct) < 32 underwent next-generation sequencing for hemagglutinin (HA) phylogenetics. Human metapneumovirus (hMPV)-positive specimens were sequenced targeting the partial F-gene for genotyping. analysis.summary_en: This study conducted molecular surveillance of respiratory viruses among outpatients with acute respiratory infections (ARI) in Yangon, Myanmar, during the 2024 rainy season. The research aimed to characterize pathogen distribution, seasonality, and genetic diversity. Nasopharyngeal swabs were tested using rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) and real-time PCR (RT-PCR) for influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2. RDT-negative specimens were analyzed with the BioFire ® FilmArray ® Respiratory 2.1 Panel (BioFire RP). Co-infections were observed in 15.3% of the specimens. Phylogenetic analysis showed distinct clustering of influenza and RSV sequences, and hMPV exhibited a genotype shift from mixed A2/B1 in 2023 to predominantly B2 in 2024. The findings emphasize the need for ongoing molecular surveillance to monitor viral evolution and circulation patterns, which are critical for public health preparedness. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational design and potential limitations in pathogen detection.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 急性呼吸道感染(ARI)仍然是热带东南亚国家缅甸的一个主要公共卫生问题,但全面的分子 监测 数据有限。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2024 年 6 月至 11 月,仰光两家医院招募了 ARI 门诊患者。我们在 2024 年雨季进行了门诊 监测 调查,并表征了病原体分布、季节性和病毒遗传多样性。
elements_zh.methods: 通过快速诊断测试 (RDT) 对鼻咽拭子进行流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和 SARS-CoV-2 筛查。RDT 阳性样本通过实时 PCR (RT-PCR) 进行确认。RDT 阴性样本使用 BioFire ® FilmArray ® Respiratory 2.1 Panel (BioFire RP) 进行测试。对循环阈值 (Ct) < 32 的甲型 (H1N1)pdm09、甲型 (H3N2) 和 B/维多利亚流感病毒进行了血凝素 (HA) 系统发育的新一代测序。hMPV 的部分 F 基因测序显示,基因型从 2023 年的 A2/B1 混合型转变为 2024 年的 B2 型为主。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 646 名 ARI 门诊患者(中位年龄 3.7 岁)中,548 名(84.8%)至少检测到一种病原体。在通过 BioFire RP 分析的 315 份 RDT 阴性样本中,鼻病毒/肠道病毒 (42.5%) 和 hMPV (15.2%) 最为常见。229 份 BioFire RP 阳性标本中,有 35 份 (15.3%) 被鉴定为合并感染。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 系统发育分析显示,甲型流感 (H3N2) 序列聚集在进化枝 J.2/J.2.1/J.2.2 内,B/Victoria 序列聚集在 V1A.3a.2(主要是 C.5.7)内,单个 A(H1N1)pdm09 序列聚集在 C.1.9 内。2024 年雨季期间,多种呼吸道病毒在此环境中共同传播,呈现出流感和 RSV 明显的季节性高峰。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 持续的病毒遗传 进化 强调了对持续分子 监测 的需求。研究结果强调了了解病毒传播模式对于改善公共卫生准备的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告与研究设计或分析方法相关的具体限制。由于该研究的观察性质和病原体检测的潜在局限性,研究结果的可信度为中等。

title: Understanding risk of poor outcomes in adults hospitalised with respiratory syncytial virus infection: evidence from a multicentre UK cohort.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes substantial winter pressure on adult services. In the UK, RSV vaccination currently targets adults aged ≥75 years and care home residents; it remains uncertain whether this age criterion alone meaningfully discriminates risk of poor outcome among adults hospitalised with RSV. METHODS: We pooled three UK hospital cohorts (one prospective, two retrospective) of adults admitted with acute respiratory infection (ARI) and PCR-confirmed RSV. The primary outcome was intensive care unit/high dependency unit (ICU/HDU) admission or all-cause mortality within 60 days. Prespecified predictors (age, sex and comorbidities) entered a least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) penalised logistic regression; selected variables were refitted using standard logistic regression. Discrimination, calibration and decision-analytic performance were assessed using 1000-bootstrap internal validation and decision-curve analysis. RESULTS: Among 334 adults, 37 (11.1%) experienced the primary outcome. An age-only rule mirroring current UK vaccine age-eligibility (≥75 years) demonstrated only modest discrimination (optimism-adjusted area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) 0.58, 95% CI 0.48 to 0.65) and a compressed distribution of predicted risks. A four-predictor model-including age, COPD, active/previous cancer and dementia-achieved higher discrimination AUC (0.77 (0.69 to 0.85)), a wider spread of predicted risks and the greatest net benefit across clinically plausible escalation thresholds (5-20%). CONCLUSIONS: In adults hospitalised with RSV-associated ARI, simple age-based heuristics-including the UK ≥75-year threshold-showed only modest ability to discriminate risk of ICU/HDU admission/60-day mortality once hospitalised. Comorbidity-inclusive approaches may provide more informative hospital-level risk stratification and warrant evaluation in future RSV vaccine-effectiveness and outcome studies. Any application requires external validation, more systematic RSV testing and comparison with physiology-based scores in larger, vaccinated cohorts.

title: Clinical and economic impact of bivalent respiratory syncytial virus prefusion F (RSVpreF) vaccination in older adults: a cost-effectiveness analysis for Chile
abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of lower respiratory tract disease in older adults in Chile. Chile's National Immunization Technical Advisory Group (NITAG) recommended RSV vaccination for adults aged ≥60 years with risk factors for severe illness. This study estimated the cost-effectiveness of bivalent RSVpreF vaccination among at-risk older adults in Chile. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: A population-based Markov model projected RSV-related outcomes under no vaccination and RSVpreF vaccination over the cohort lifetime. Cost-effectiveness was assessed from healthcare and societal perspectives in 2025 Chilean Pesos (CLP) and US Dollars (US$), with costs and outcomes discounted at 3% annually. Sensitivity analyses tested the model robustness. RESULTS: RSVpreF vaccination was projected to prevent 14,956 hospitalizations, 50,419 emergency department visits, and 124,849 physician office visits; avert CLP76 billion (US$82 million) in direct medical costs and CLP305 billion (US$328 million) in indirect costs; and generate 7,079 quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs). At a threshold of CLP15,977,348 (US$17,180) per QALY gained, the maximum cost-effective vaccine price was CLP100,480 (US$108) and CLP265,261 (US$285) from the healthcare and societal perspectives respectively. CONCLUSIONS: RSVpreF vaccination would reduce RSV burden and likely be cost-effective for older adults in Chile.

title: Association between 12 common respiratory pathogens and Streptococcus pneumoniae detection among hospitalized children in Hainan, and characterization of antimicrobial resistance and molecular epidemiology in pneumococcal isolates
abstract: Data from the COVID-19 pandemic demonstrated a strong association between reduced invasive pneumococcal disease and decreased circulation of specific respiratory viruses. However, studies investigating the association between common respiratory pathogens and Streptococcus pneumoniae ( S. pneumoniae ) detection rates remain limited, and molecular epidemiology data for pediatric S. pneumoniae infections in Hainan are lacking. From July 2021 to June 2025, we retrospectively analyzed the detection profiles of 12 common respiratory pathogens in hospitalized children. Spearman correlation was used to examine the relationship between each pathogen’s monthly detection rate and its co-detection rate with S. Separately, 434 consecutive S. pneumoniae isolates collected from May 2023 to April 2024 underwent Quellung serotyping, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and whole-genome sequencing. During the study period, S. pneumoniae detection rates among hospitalized children in Hainan ranged from 20% to 40% without a clear seasonal pattern, but were higher during strict COVID-19 lockdowns than after policy relaxation. Positive ecological correlations were observed between S. pneumoniae detection rates and 12 common respiratory pathogen circulation. Age-stratified analysis revealed distinct correlation patterns: HMPV, IAV, RSV, and CoV showed the strongest associations with S. pneumoniae co-detection in children aged 0–3 years; M. pneumoniae , HMPV, HRV, and RSV in those aged 4–6 years; and IAV, IBV, AdV, and HMPV in those aged 7–18 years. pneumoniae isolates, 21 serotypes and 85 sequence types (24 novel) were identified. The six most prevalent serotypes were 19 F, 6B, 23 F, 19 A, 6 A, and 15 A, with ST271 as the dominant sequence type. All non-meningitis isolates were penicillin-susceptible at non-meningitis breakpoints, and serotype 19 F exhibited the highest antimicrobial resistance rates. PCV13 and PPV23 covered 78.3% and 76.5% of isolates, respectively. A 13.8% discordance rate was observed between Quellung serotyping and molecular serotyping, with discrepancies concentrated in serogroup 6. Additional discrepancies arose when molecular serotyping results were compared across different platforms. Our findings suggest that the circulation of RSV, M. pneumoniae , HMPV, HRV, and influenza viruses may influence S. pneumoniae detection in hospitalized children. These findings pertain to this clinical population and should not be extrapolated to colonization rates in healthy individuals. Finally, accurate pneumococcal surveillance in the post-vaccine era would benefit from integrating genomic and traditional phenotypic approaches.

source_records.abstract: Data from the COVID-19 pandemic demonstrated a strong association between reduced invasive pneumococcal disease and decreased circulation of specific respiratory viruses. However, studies investigating the association between common respiratory pathogens and Streptococcus pneumoniae ( S. pneumoniae ) detection rates remain limited, and molecular epidemiology data for pediatric S. pneumoniae infections in Hainan are lacking. From July 2021 to June 2025, we retrospectively analyzed the detection profiles of 12 common respiratory pathogens in hospitalized children. Spearman correlation was used to examine the relationship between each pathogen’s monthly detection rate and its co-detection rate with S. Separately, 434 consecutive S. pneumoniae isolates collected from May 2023 to April 2024 underwent Quellung serotyping, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and whole-genome sequencing. During the study period, S. pneumoniae detection rates among hospitalized children in Hainan ranged from 20% to 40% without a clear seasonal pattern, but were higher during strict COVID-19 lockdowns than after policy relaxation. Positive ecological correlations were observed between S. pneumoniae detection rates and 12 common respiratory pathogen circulation. Age-stratified analysis revealed distinct correlation patterns: HMPV, IAV, RSV, and CoV showed the strongest associations with S. pneumoniae co-detection in children aged 0–3 years; M. pneumoniae , HMPV, HRV, and RSV in those aged 4–6 years; and IAV, IBV, AdV, and HMPV in those aged 7–18 years. pneumoniae isolates, 21 serotypes and 85 sequence types (24 novel) were identified. These findings pertain to this clinical population and should not be extrapolated to colonization rates in healthy individuals. Finally, accurate pneumococcal surveillance in the post-vaccine era would benefit from integrating genomic and traditional phenotypic approaches.

abstract_zh: COVID-19 大流行的数据表明,侵袭性肺炎球菌疾病减少与特定呼吸道病毒循环减少之间存在密切关联。然而,调查常见呼吸道病原体与肺炎链球菌检出率之间关系的研究仍然有限,并且缺乏海南儿童肺炎链球菌感染的分子 流行病学 数据。回顾性分析2021年7月至2025年6月住院儿童12种常见呼吸道病原体的检测情况。采用 Spearman 相关性检验每种病原体的月检出率及其与链球菌的共检出率之间的关系。另外,对 2023 年 5 月至 2024 年 4 月连续收集的 434 株肺炎链球菌分离株进行了 Quellung 血清分型、药敏检测和全 基因组 测序。研究期间,海南省住院儿童的肺炎链球菌检出率在20%至40%之间,没有明显的季节性模式,但在严格的COVID-19封锁期间比政策放松后更高。肺炎链球菌检出率与 12 种常见呼吸道病原体循环之间存在正生态相关性。年龄分层分析揭示了不同的相关模式:HMPV、IAV、RSV 和 CoV 在 0-3 岁儿童中与肺炎链球菌联合检测的关联性最强;4-6岁儿童肺炎支原体、HMPV、HRV和RSV;7-18 岁人群的 IAV、IBV、AdV 和 HMPV。肺炎链球菌分离株,已鉴定出 21 种血清型和 85 种序列类型(其中 24 种是新的)。六种最流行的血清型是 19 F、6B、23 F、19 A、6 A 和 15 A,其中 ST271 为主要序列类型。所有非脑膜炎分离株在非脑膜炎断点处均对青霉素敏感,血清型 19 F 表现出最高的抗菌素耐药率。PCV13 和 PPV23 分别覆盖了 78.3% 和 76.5% 的分离株。Quellung 血清分型和分子血清分型之间存在 13.8% 的不一致率,差异集中在血清组 6。当在不同平台上比较分子血清分型结果时,还出现了其他差异。我们的研究结果表明,RSV、肺炎支原体、HMPV、HRV 和流感病毒的传播可能会影响住院儿童中肺炎链球菌的检测。这些发现适用于该临床人群,不应推断健康个体的定植率。最后,后 疫苗 时代准确的肺炎球菌 疫苗 将受益于基因组和传统表型方法的整合。

title: Molecular epidemiology of respiratory syncytial virus infections in Arizona, USA during the 2023-24 and 2024-25 seasons
abstract: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus infection is a common cause of hospitalizations in infants and elderly patients. With the increased availability of vaccines and therapeutic antibodies, surveilling the sequence landscape of viral genomes is important to increase awareness of potentially neutralizing mutations. During the 2023-24 and 2024-25 RSV seasons, we collected unpaired nasopharyngeal swab specimens from patients presenting to Arizona healthcare systems with symptoms of influenza-like illness. Using either tiled amplicon-based enrichment or a commercial oligo hybrid-enrichment panel and next generation sequencing, we obtained genome sequences for RSV and co-infecting viruses. We performed phylogenetic and genomic analyses to classify RSV genomes and detect mutations in the antigenic sites of the F protein and conserved central domain of the G protein. abstract: Background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and influenza can both cause severe viral pneumonia requiring intensive care. Influenza is supported by established vaccination programs and antiviral therapy, whereas outcomes of RSV infection among critically ill adults remain less well characterized. This study compared clinical presentation, treatment, and outcomes between ICU admissions classified as RSV pneumonia and those classified as influenza pneumonia. Methods: A retrospective cohort was assembled from MIMIC-IV data covering 2008–2019. The analytical cohort comprised 201 infection-specific ICU observations classified as RSV pneumonia (n = 40) or influenza pneumonia (n = 161). title: Burden of Pneumonia in Older Adults and the Role of Immunization
abstract: Lower respiratory infections remain the leading infectious cause of death worldwide, with pneumonia causing a substantial burden of morbidity, mortality, and long-term complications in older adults, particularly among those with chronic comorbidities, immunocompromising conditions, or those living in nursing homes. Streptococcus pneumoniae remains the leading bacterial pathogen, while influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) are major viral causes of pneumonia and may predispose individuals to secondary bacterial infection. Vaccination is the cornerstone of prevention. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines and vaccines against influenza, COVID-19, and RSV reduce clinically relevant respiratory outcomes in older adults, although the strength of evidence and the endpoints evaluated differ among vaccines. However, vaccination coverage remains suboptimal because of limited awareness, vaccine hesitancy, differences in immunization policies, and barriers to healthcare access. Improving vaccine uptake through life-course immunization strategies, strong recommendations from healthcare professionals, and equitable access could help reduce pneumonia burden among older adults.

title: Healthcare resource use and costs following RSV-related hospitalizations among US adults aged 50 years and older.
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), a common virus causing acute respiratory illness (ARI), can lead to severe disease among adults aged ≥50 y. We assessed healthcare resource utilization (HRU) and costs among United States (US) adults aged ≥50 y after hospitalization with RSV-ARI. Using 2015-2023 US claims data from the Optum® Clinformatics® Data Mart, three cohorts of patients aged ≥50 y were identified: patients with ≥1 RSV-ARI episode involving hospitalization (RSV-ARI cohort), patients with ≥1 influenza-ARI episode involving hospitalization (influenza-ARI cohort), and patients without recent ARI (control cohort). HRU and costs per-patient-per-month (PPPM) were assessed at 30 d, 3 months, and 1 y post-index. Adjusted regression models compared outcomes across cohorts. Overall, 14,759 patients were included in the RSV-ARI cohort, 77,468 in the influenza-ARI cohort, and 73,795 in the control cohort. The RSV-ARI cohort had significantly higher HRU vs. controls within 1 y post-index; adjusted incidence rate ratios (95% confidence interval) 30 d through 1 y post-index ranged from 81.07 (75.85, 86.65) to 11.56 (11.20, 11.93) for inpatient stays, 5.93 (5.58, 6.30) to 2.19 (2.09, 2.29) for emergency department visits, and 1.99 (1.95, 2.04) to 1.78 (1.75, 1.81) for outpatient visits. Adjusted total costs PPPM were higher for the RSV-ARI cohort vs. controls post-index (difference at 30 d: $37,025 [$36,345, $37,704]; 1 y: $6,699 [$6,476, $6,922]). HRU and costs among patients aged ≥50 y with RSV-ARI were higher vs. controls and generally similar between the RSV-ARI and influenza-ARI cohorts, demonstrating economic burden of severe RSV disease and the importance of RSV prevention.

title: Epidemic Evolution and Research Progress of Pathogenic Viruses Causing Respiratory Tract Infections After 2020
abstract: Respiratory tract infections are among the most common infectious diseases worldwide. Since 2020, the epidemiological characteristics of respiratory infections have changed significantly under the influence of various factors, posing persistent challenges to global public health and human health. This study reviews changes in the epidemiological characteristics of major respiratory pathogenic viruses since 2020 and related research advances using literature analysis and comparative analysis. The findings indicate that the overall positive detection rates of respiratory syncytial virus, rhinovirus, and influenza virus have declined to some extent, but these viruses remain major pathogens of respiratory infections. Children and older adults are the primary susceptible populations, with different viruses exhibiting distinct age distributions and seasonal patterns. Multiple factors have contributed to changes in the epidemiology of respiratory viruses, and mixed infections involving multiple pathogens have become an important contributor to disease complexity. In recent years, advances in viral detection and surveillance technologies have provided support for accurate diagnosis and disease prevention and control.

title: Post-acute symptom persistence following SARS-CoV-2, RSV, and influenza in children: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Persistent symptoms following acute viral respiratory infections are increasingly recognized in children. While post-acute sequelae of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2; long COVID) have been extensively studied, whether comparable post-acute morbidity occurs after other major respiratory viruses and whether clinical patterns differ across pathogens remains incompletely characterized. This retrospective cohort study included children aged 0 to 18 years with reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 (n = 1540), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; n = 2150), or influenza (n = 2050) infections evaluated between January 2020 and December 2024 at a tertiary university hospital system in Istanbul, Turkey. Persistent symptoms were assessed at clinician-documented follow-up visits 4 to 6 weeks after virological diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors for each pathogen. Bonferroni correction was applied for multiple comparisons. Model calibration was assessed using the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and discriminative ability by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. Among 5740 children, persistent symptoms at 4 to 6 weeks were documented in 24.0% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 22.2-25.8) with RSV, 22.0% (95% CI = 19.9-24.1) with SARS-CoV-2, and 21.2% (95% CI = 19.4-23.0) with influenza (P = .086). While overall post-acute prevalence was comparable across the 3 viruses, symptom profiles differed markedly: RSV-related post-acute morbidity was dominated by respiratory and feeding difficulties in young infants; SARS-CoV-2 predominantly produced neurocognitive and systemic complaints in school-aged children; and influenza was characterized by sustained systemic symptoms. Hypoxemia was the strongest predictor for RSV (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 2.4, 95% CI = 1.7-3.3), while age >6 years (aOR = 2.1, 95% CI = 1.5-2.9) and hospitalization (aOR = 1.9, 95% CI = 1.4-2.6) were leading predictors for SARS-CoV-2. Age-stratified analyses demonstrated a significant virus × age interaction (P .05). Inverse probability weighting sensitivity analysis yielded consistent results. Post-acute symptom persistence following pediatric viral respiratory infections is common and follows virus-specific patterns. Overall post-acute symptom prevalence was comparable across the 3 viruses, but symptom profiles were strikingly virus-specific and age-dependent. This direct comparison of 3 major respiratory viruses demonstrates that post-acute morbidity extends beyond SARS-CoV-2 and varies by pathogen and age. These findings support the development of pathogen-informed follow-up considerations.

This direct comparison of 3 major respiratory viruses demonstrates that post-acute morbidity extends beyond SARS-CoV-2 and varies by pathogen and age. These findings support the development of pathogen-informed follow-up considerations.

full_text: Abstract Background The COVID-19 pandemic has altered the epidemic patterns of human metapneumovirus (hMPV) globally. As no licensed prophylactic products currently exist for hMPV, understanding population immunity is essential for identifying susceptible groups and informing prevention strategies. This study aimed to quantify age-specific hMPV neutralizing antibody (NAb) levels and seroprevalence in the postpandemic period. Methods We analyzed serum samples collected in a previously published community-based cross-sectional sero-epidemiological survey conducted in Taizhou city, eastern China, from June 2 to June 30, 2024, using a multistage, age-stratified sampling design with additional oversampling of children aged < 5 years. Serum samples were tested for hMPV NAb levels via a fluorescence-based microneutralization assay, with seropositivity defined as a titer of 1:30. We estimated geometric mean titers (GMTs) and seroprevalence rates across age groups. Factors associated with the NAb titer were examined using generalized linear models. We also examined the relationship between RSV- and hMPV-specific antibody responses, given their potential cross-reactivity. Results A total of 1303 participants aged 16 months to 93 years were included. Antibody levels were lowest among children aged 16 to < 36 months (GMT: 217, 95% CI: 159–295). The GMTs increased to 331 among children aged 3–4 years and exceeded 1000 among those aged 5–11 years, remaining elevated throughout life. The highest GMTs were observed in adults aged 65 years and older (1829, 95% CI: 1620–2064). Among children aged < 5 years, NAb titers increased by 74.7% (95% CI: 14.4%–167.0%) for each additional year of age. Approximately 67.8% (137/202) of the participants were seropositive in the age groups of 16 to < 36 months. From 6 years onward, the seroprevalence was close to or reached 100%. Higher RSV prefusion F IgG antibody titers were significantly associated with higher hMPV NAb titers (Spearman’s ρ: 0.302, P < 0.001), which may reflect shared epidemiological exposures, individual differences in immune responses, or possible cross-reactive immunity between the two viruses. Conclusions This study provides population-based evidence of age-specific hMPV NAb patterns in the post-COVID-19 pandemic period. The relatively low seroprevalence in children aged 16 to < 36 months highlights the importance of continued hMPV surveillance in this potentially susceptible population. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to quantify age-specific hMPV neutralizing antibody (NAb) levels and seroprevalence in the postpandemic period. Abstract Background The COVID-19 pandemic has altered the epidemic patterns of human metapneumovirus (hMPV) globally.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional seroepidemiological study was conducted in Taizhou city, eastern China, from June 2 to June 30, 2024, using a multistage, age-stratified sampling design with additional oversampling of children aged < 5 years. Results A total of 1303 participants aged 16 months to 93 years were included.
analysis.methods: Serum samples were tested for hMPV NAb levels via a fluorescence-based microneutralization assay, with seropositivity defined as a titer of 1:30. We estimated geometric mean titers (GMTs) and seroprevalence rates across age groups.
analysis.main_results: Antibody levels were lowest among children aged 16 to < 36 months (GMT: 217, 95% CI: 159–295). The GMTs increased to 331 among children aged 3–4 years and exceeded 1000 among those aged 5–11 years, remaining elevated throughout life. The highest GMTs were observed in adults aged 65 years and older (1829, 95% CI: 1620–2064). Among children aged < 5 years, NAb titers increased by 74.7% (95% CI: 14.4%–167.0%) for each additional year of age.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This study provides population-based evidence of age-specific hMPV NAb patterns in the post-COVID-19 pandemic period. The relatively low seroprevalence in children aged 16 to < 36 months highlights the importance of continued hMPV surveillance in this potentially susceptible population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for targeted hMPV surveillance and prevention strategies, particularly in children aged 16 to < 36 months who show lower seroprevalence. The study also suggests that understanding immune responses to related viruses like RSV may provide insights into hMPV immunity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality. The evidence is moderate, as the results are based on a single geographic location and time period, and the association with RSV antibodies is speculative.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional seroepidemiological study in Taizhou city, eastern China, investigated age-specific neutralizing antibody (NAb) levels against human metapneumovirus (hMPV) in the post-COVID-19 pandemic period. The study analyzed serum samples collected from June 2 to June 30, 2024, using a multistage, age-stratified sampling design. Results showed that antibody levels were lowest among children aged 16 to < 36 months, with geometric mean titers (GMTs) increasing with age. The highest GMTs were observed in adults aged 65 years and older. The study highlights the importance of continued hMPV surveillance in children, as their seroprevalence remains relatively low. The findings suggest that understanding immune responses to related viruses like RSV may provide insights into hMPV immunity. However, the study is limited by its cross-sectional design and geographic focus, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到横截面设计的限制,无法确定因果关系。证据是中等的,因为结果是基于单一地理位置和时间段,并且与 RSV 抗体的关联是推测性的。

title: Epidemiology of respiratory pathogens and expanded panel testing in influenza-like illness and severe acute respiratory infection in Changsha, central China
abstract: Post-pandemic respiratory pathogen circulation in central China remains insufficiently characterized across influenza-like illness (ILI) and severe acute respiratory infection (SARI). We analyzed 11,355 patients from seven sentinel hospitals in Changsha between October 2023 and March 2026. Patients underwent multiplex nucleic acid testing for a 12-pathogen core panel, expanded to a 15-pathogen analytical panel in 2025. Overall, 50.64% tested positive for at least one pathogen, most commonly for Streptococcus pneumoniae (SP) (14.51%), influenza virus (10.82%), and rhinovirus (7.38%). Pathogens circulated asynchronously, with a marked influenza rebound, intermittent SARS-CoV-2 waves, delayed respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) resurgence, and recurrent rhinovirus/enterovirus activity. Most respiratory viruses predominated in young children, Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) peaked in adolescents and young adults, SARS-CoV-2 positivity increased with age, and SP showed a U-shaped age pattern. Compared with ILI, SARI showed higher adjusted odds of MP, RSV, and SP detection. Co-detections clustered in children and were mainly viral–bacterial. Expanding the detection panel increased positivity from 55.20% to 62.97% and co-detection from 12.80% to 23.31%. These findings provide evidence to guide integrated multi-pathogen surveillance and context-specific panel expansion in the post-COVID era.

Introduction Acute respiratory infections (ARIs) remain a major cause of outpatient visits, hospitalization, and seasonal pressure on health services1. Their clinical manifestations overlap substantially, but the underlying etiology spans a broad range of viral, atypical, and bacterial pathogens2. This makes routine interpretation difficult when surveillance is limited to a single pathogen or a single syndrome3. A nationwide surveillance study in China has already shown that pathogen distribution differs markedly by age and clinical presentation, while more recent all-age surveillance in Zhejiang further highlighted that infection and co-infection patterns vary across age groups and are linked to different risks of pneumonia3,4. Together, these findings suggest that routine respiratory surveillance needs to move beyond single-pathogen reporting toward a broader etiological view3,4. This need has become even clearer in the post-pandemic period. During the COVID-19 pandemic, non- pharmaceutical interventions suppressed not only SARS-CoV-2 transmission but also the circulation of other respiratory pathogens5. Their return after the relaxation of these measures has not followed a simple “return to normal” pattern, with recent studies describing altered seasonality, out-of-season activity, and changes in population susceptibility after the lifting of NPIs5. In Guangdong, sentinel multi- pathogen surveillance during the first post-pandemic year found that influenza activity started earlier than in the pre-COVID period and that MP re-emerged after a period of suppression6. In Ningbo, overall pathogen activity rose markedly in 2023 compared with 2020–2022, accompanied by increases in influenza, HMPV, HPIV, HCoV, and MP, as well as more co-infections7. These studies suggest that post- Page 2/24 pandemic respiratory epidemiology is being reshaped by altered seasonality, wave replacement, and changing age susceptibility rather than by a simple restoration of pre-pandemic circulation5–7. Age and clinical syndrome are notable contributing dimensions for post-pandemic respiratory surveillance. In Zhejiang, age-specific analysis showed that different pathogens cluster in different parts of the life course, and that MP is particularly prominent among adolescents with pneumonia4. In Suzhou, pediatric hospitalization data collected after the end of the zero-COVID policy showed a sharp rise in overall pathogen positivity, with marked increases in RSV, influenza, HRV, HPIV, and MP, especially in younger children8. These studies make two points that are directly relevant to the present study: overall positivity alone is not enough to describe post-pandemic respiratory activity, and age and disease severity need to be built into surveillance interpretation from the outset4,8. Another gap is more practical than epidemiological. Most recent Chinese studies have relied on a fixed testing panel—12 pathogens in Guangdong, 13 in Zhejiang, 10 in Ningbo, and 9 in the Suzhou pediatric study—and have mainly used these panels to describe when pathogens circulated and which age groups were prominently affected4,6–8. Much less is known about how surveillance results change when the panel itself changes, although broader multiplex diagnostic literature emphasizes that expanded panels can alter microbiological yield, co-detection patterns, and interpretation of respiratory infection data9,10. This matters in practice because adding only a small number of targets, especially bacterial targets, may have a limited effect on headline positivity while substantially altering the apparent burden of co- detection and, with it, the way surveillance data are interpreted9,10. Direct within-system evidence from China on the incremental diagnostic yield of panel expansion remains limited. At the same time, central China is still less well described than coastal regions. Within Hunan, recent multicenter evidence has focused mainly on pediatric patients with acute respiratory tract infections, leaving routine all-age ILI/SARI sentinel surveillance in this region less clearly defined11. Against this background, we used routine surveillance data from seven sentinel hospitals in Changsha to characterize the post-pandemic epidemiological patterns of core respiratory pathogens in ILI and SARI cases. We aimed not only to provide local epidemiological evidence from central China on temporal variation, age-specific detection patterns, and co-infection structure, but also to address a practical surveillance question that has received less attention: how much additional information is gained when routine monitoring expands from a 12-pathogen core panel to a 15-pathogen panel. Results A total of 11,355 patients were included, comprising 8,660 influenza-like illness (ILI) cases and 2,695 severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) cases. Overall, 50.64% (5,750/11,355) tested positive for at least one respiratory pathogen. Because not all specimens were assayed for every target, pathogen- specific denominators varied. Among those tested, SP had the highest overall positivity (14.51%, 1,410/9,715), followed by IFV (10.82%, 1,229/11,355) and rhinovirus (7.38%, 834/11,299). Overall Page 3/24 positivity was almost identical in ILI and SARI (50.48% vs 51.13%), but the pathogen profile differed. In ILI, the most frequently detected pathogens were SP, IFV, and SARS-CoV-2, whereas in SARI they were SP, RSV, and rhinovirus. SARI was concentrated in children aged ≤ 5 years and older adults aged ≥ 60 years, whereas ILI was more common in adolescents and adults aged 18–59 years; females were more frequently represented in SARI than in ILI (61.41% vs 50.60%). Chlamydia pneumoniae (CP) was rarely detected (15/3,281, 0.46%) and had limited evaluable data for robust subgroup analyses, therefore, it was excluded from subsequent stratified, temporal, and co-detection analyses (Table 1). After adjustment for sentinel hospital, age and sex, SARI remained positively associated with MP (aOR, 4.81; 95% CI, 3.66–6.32), RSV (aOR, 1.92; 95% CI, 1.62–2.27), and SP (aOR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.11–1.44) detection compared with ILI cases. Lower odds in SARI were observed for HCoV, SARS-CoV-2, IFV, and ADV detection, whereas no significant adjusted differences were observed for RV, HPIV, EV, HMPV, or HBoV (Table 2). We plotted the monthly positive counts and test positivity for 12 respiratory pathogens over the surveillance period from October 2023 to March 2026 (Fig. 1). SP was detected throughout the study period, with an early peak in January 2024 followed by persistent moderate activity. IFV showed the clearest seasonal signal, with activity in late 2023/early 2024, a smaller resurgence in early 2025, and a major rebound at the end of 2025, when positivity reached 44.58%, the highest level observed during surveillance. SARS-CoV-2 showed two distinct waves, peaking in March 2024 and again in spring- summer 2025, before declining toward lower activity. RSV remained relatively low through most of 2024 but rose in 2025, reaching 16.05% late in the year. RV and EV circulated in repeated waves, whereas ADV and MP were concentrated mainly in the early part of surveillance. HPIV, HMPV, and HCoV showed smaller intermittent peaks, and HBoV remained uncommon throughout. Nonlinear age-specific patterns in pathogen positivity were observed (Fig. 2). SARS-CoV-2 positivity increased with age, particularly in ILI, with a modest rise in early adulthood followed by a more pronounced increase in older adults. IFV showed a different pattern: in ILI, positivity peaked in adolescents and young adults and then declined, whereas in SARI it increased more steadily with age and became relatively more prominent in older adults. By contrast, RSV, ADV, HMPV, HPIV, HCoV, rhinovirus, and enterovirus were concentrated in young children and declined with age, although small Page 6/24 late-life upturns were visible for RSV in SARI and for HMPV and HPIV in ILI. HBoV remained uncommon across the age range. MP showed the sharpest age concentration, with a pronounced peak in adolescents and young adults that was substantially higher in SARI than in ILI, followed by a steep decline. SP showed a U-shaped distribution, with high positivity in infancy, a trough in mid-adulthood, and a secondary rise in older age, especially in SARI. The age-specific shapes were broadly similar between ILI and SARI, but the magnitude differed by syndrome. Among the 9,715 patients with complete results for all 12 core pathogens, 1,195 (12.30%) had co- detections. Viral-bacterial co-detection was the dominant pattern overall (9.07%), whereas viral-viral and bacterial-bacterial co-detections were much less common (2.89% and 0.34%, respectively). Co-detection showed a strong age gradient, peaking in children aged ≤ 5 years (21.82%) and then falling sharply in adults and older adults; differences across age groups were significant for overall co-detection and for each co-detection subtype (all P < 0.001). Male patients had higher overall, viral-viral, and viral-bacterial co-detection rates than female patients, whereas bacterial-bacterial co-detection did not differ by sex. SARI cases had a higher overall co-detection rate than ILI cases (14.95% vs 11.39%), driven mainly by viral-bacterial (10.84% vs 8.46%, P < 0.001) and bacterial-bacterial (0.77% vs 0.19%, P < 0.001) combinations; viral-viral co-detection rates were similar in the two groups (Table 3). In ILI cases, the leading co-detection pairs were IFV-SP, RV-SP, and RSV-SP, with corresponding rates of 2.00%, 1.44%, and 1.18%, respectively. By comparison, SARI cases more commonly exhibited RSV-SP, RV-SP, and HPIV-SP co-detections, occurring at rates of 3.02%, 2.18%, and 1.89%, respectively (Fig. 3). In both syndromes, the co-detection network was centered on SP, although the associated viral partners differed, suggesting that pathogen interplay may not be the same in milder outpatient illness and more severe hospitalized disease. Among the 4,569 specimens collected from 2025 to March 2026 with complete results for all 15 analytical pathogens, expanding the panel from 12 to 15 targets increased any-pathogen positivity from 55.20% to 62.97%, an absolute increase of 7.77 percentage points. Monoinfection fell from 42.39% to 39.66%, whereas co-detection rose from 12.80% to 23.31%, an absolute increase of 10.51 percentage points. Among specimens classified as negative by the 12-pathogen core panel, the expanded panel Page 8/24 identified 355 additional positives (17.34%). Among specimens classified as monoinfections by the core panel, 470 (24.26%) were reclassified as co-detections after panel expansion. Most of this increase was driven by the addition of bacterial targets, particularly HP (Table 4). Overall, these findings indicate that the incremental diagnostic yield of expanded surveillance in 2025 was substantial and was driven predominantly by the inclusion of additional bacterial targets, particularly HP.
